decisions.label: Plain-text corpus
decisions.detail: Wikipedia's explaintext API for the "India" article in each language — flattened prose, no headings/bold/links/tables.

decisions.label: Whitespace pre-tokenizer
decisions.detail: Splits punctuation off words ("India," → "India" + ",") before training.

decisions.label: Lowercase normalizer
decisions.detail: Collapses case variants ("India"/"india") into one atom — a real, free fertility win for English.

decisions.label: Explicit [UNK] token
decisions.detail: An unrecognized character becomes a real, visible, counted [UNK] token rather than vanishing.

decisions.label: Hindi + Marathi trained jointly
decisions.detail: They share Devanagari script. Training them independently and then combining the two vocabularies corrupts merge priority order — verified empirically (Marathi's fertility got measurably worse after a naive merge). Training them together as one pool avoids this.

decisions.label: 3 script-safe groups, merged into one vocab
decisions.detail: English (Latin), Telugu (Telugu script), and the Hindi+Marathi pool (Devanagari) are trained separately, then their vocabularies are concatenated into one final tokenizer — safe because none of the three scripts overlap.

decisions.label: English gets the minimum budget it needs, first
decisions.detail: English's fertility must be < 1.2. Vocab search finds the smallest English allocation that clears that bar, then spends 100% of what's left equalizing Telugu and Hindi+Marathi as tightly as possible.

decisions.label: Fertility metric: per unique word
decisions.detail: Tokens needed to encode each distinct word once, divided by the number of distinct words. A word used once counts the same as one used 50 times.

cons.label: Not round-trip safe
cons.detail: No decoder is configured, and Whitespace's split destroys the information needed to reconstruct it: decode(encode(text)) inserts stray spaces around punctuation ("India," → "India ,") and even between subword pieces of the same word ("hello" → "hel lo").

cons.label: Case is unrecoverable
cons.detail: Lowercase normalization means "India" always decodes back as "india" — the original casing is gone for good.

cons.label: Fertility can never drop below ~1.0 per word
cons.detail: Whitespace's atom boundaries mean no single token can ever cover more than one word-unit, unlike v2's Metaspace.

cons.label: Per-word metric penalizes rare vocabulary
cons.detail: Since every distinct word counts equally regardless of frequency, long-tail rare words drag the average up — getting every language's fertility below 1.2 within one shared 10,000-token budget turned out to be mathematically infeasible (would need ~16,500 tokens even with every optimization tried).
